items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: That’s why somebody like John Williams, who sits there and just writes and then “Star Wars” comes out or something.

ctx.x: Did your confidence that your arrangements, your orchestrations, were going to work increase over the years? I’m thinking about those moments where you write a chart especially pre-computer, and you work for hours and days on it and the first time it gets played and you’ve got your fingers crossed. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

Yeah. They call it the “cringe moment.” So you’d better be hearing what you’re hearing. That’s why somebody like John Williams, who sits there and just writes and then “Star Wars” comes out or something. You know it’s like that’s their instrument, you know what I mean? Nelson Riddle. That’s his instrument. For me I had to battle with the piano being my instrument, and finding a way to break away from it. You know now I come back to it, as I said before, and it is my slave. Because I’m not hearing that, I’m…
Well your orchestral pieces are not necessarily realizations of your piano compositions. Is that a correct statement?
